How does a business get mentioned in ChatGPT and Google's AI answers?

Let the right crawlers in, publish clear answers to real questions, keep your details consistent and earn mentions elsewhere. No file or markup guarantees a citation.

By Taz Abbas, Managing Partner · Published October 29, 2026 · Digital Presence

The short answer

AI answer tools such as ChatGPT search and Google's AI Overviews build their answers from web pages they can find, read and trust. So the path to being mentioned is the same path that leads to good search visibility: let their crawlers in, publish clear pages that answer specific questions, keep your business details consistent everywhere, and earn mentions on other sites. There is no special file or markup that guarantees a citation, and anyone who promises one is overselling.

How AI answers find their sources

When someone asks an AI search tool a question, it typically runs searches, reads the pages that come back and writes an answer, often with links to the pages it used. Google says its AI features draw on pages that are indexed and eligible to appear in Search with a snippet, and that there are no additional requirements or special optimizations needed to appear in them. OpenAI says any public website can appear in ChatGPT search, provided its search crawler is not blocked.

In practice, that means two things matter most: being reachable and indexable, and being the clearest, most trustworthy answer to the question being asked.

Traditional search still matters

It is tempting to treat AI answers as a separate channel that needs a separate strategy. For most businesses it is better to see them as another way people search. The same pages that rank well and earn clicks from ordinary search results are the ones AI tools tend to read and cite. If your site is not yet indexed in Google and Bing, start there, because an AI tool that relies on search results cannot cite a page those results do not include.

1. Let the right crawlers in

Check your robots.txt file and your security settings. Search crawlers such as Googlebot and Bingbot must be allowed. For ChatGPT search, OpenAI's search crawler, OAI-SearchBot, must not be blocked. Other AI search tools have their own crawlers.

There is a distinction worth knowing. Some AI crawlers collect content to train models, while others fetch pages to cite them in answers. Many businesses choose to block training crawlers while allowing search crawlers. That is a reasonable policy, but make it deliberately, because blocking the wrong ones can remove you from AI answers your buyers see.

2. Publish pages that answer real questions

AI tools quote passages that answer a question directly. Pages that bury the answer in marketing language are hard to quote. Write the way your buyers ask:

  • Use the question as a heading, then answer it in the first two or three sentences.
  • Follow with the detail: steps, comparisons, conditions and exceptions.
  • Cover one topic per page, so it is clear what the page is about.
  • Keep important content in text, not only in images or videos.
  • Say who wrote it and when it was updated, and keep it current.

Service pages should say plainly who you serve, what you do, where you work and how to contact you. An AI tool asked for "channel consultants for companies entering the US" can only suggest you if a page states that clearly.

3. Keep your details consistent everywhere

AI tools cross-check facts. If your website, Google Business Profile, LinkedIn page and directory listings describe your business, location and services differently, the tools have less confidence in any of them. Use the same name, the same description of what you do and the same contact details across every profile you control. Structured data on your website, such as organization details, helps search engines read these facts, but it must match what the page visibly says.

4. Earn mentions on other sites

AI answers lean on what other sources say about you, not just what you say about yourself. Mentions in industry publications, association listings, partner websites, podcasts and conference pages all help, especially when they describe what you do in the same words you use. Reviews on relevant platforms count too. This is slow work, but it compounds.

5. Measure what you can

Measurement is still imperfect. Google includes traffic from its AI features in Search Console's performance report. ChatGPT adds a source tag to links it sends, so visits from ChatGPT show in most analytics tools. Beyond that, the most practical check is to ask the tools the questions your buyers ask, every month or so, and note whether you appear and which pages are cited.

What not to do

  • Do not publish large volumes of thin pages written only to target AI tools. Search engines treat that as spam.
  • Do not add hidden text or markup that says something the page does not.
  • Do not pay for services that guarantee placement in AI answers. No one controls that.

A practical plan

Fix access first, then rewrite your key service pages so each states clearly who it is for and what you do. Add a steady stream of question-led articles in your area of expertise. Tidy your business profiles so they match. Then build mentions on sites your buyers already read. The businesses that show up in AI answers are, for the most part, the ones that have done the basics of being found online well.
